Expected results

  • Step 4: the lead changes at once with the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-D}", with an Undo button, and no "Clear … scheduled shifts?" question ({Technician-A} has no shift on this work order); the card moves to {Technician-D}'s column.
  • Steps 7 and 9: {Line-1} now follows {Technician-D}, and {Technician-B} is still listed among {Line-1}'s technicians.
  • Steps 7 and 12: {Line-2} still has {Technician-C} as its technician; it did not move to {Technician-D}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), the context note under S4-R8 (added in version 46, 12 Oct 2026, after SV-11128), the S4-R8 line table, S4-R5 (message wording changed in versions 66 and 68, 19 Oct 2026) and S4-R28 (reworded in version 49 on 14 Oct 2026 from Chris Ward's answer 1 of 14 Oct 2026; {Technician-A} has no shift on this work order, so the question still does not open), read 19 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Re-read against PRD version 82 (29 Oct 2026) on 2 Nov 2026: the quoted rules are unchanged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”
  • S4-R28: “The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line of the work order, judged at the moment the lead changes; this is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. Lines not yet approved, and declined lines, are ignored. On a work order with one line, a shift on that line counts, and so does a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line. A shift on only some approved lines does not show the prompt, and that includes an Entire work order shift once a line has been added and approved after it was made.”
  • S4-R8 context note (SV-11128): “"Explicitly assigned" means the line's own technician, set through Edit Line. A technician who is on a line only because of a Schedule shift, whether the shift was dropped on that line or on the entire work order, does not count: the line follows the incoming lead like any other line, and the shift technician stays on the line's technician list.”
  • S4-R8 table: explicit: “Explicitly assigned to a different technician | No — the explicit assignment is preserved”

Last checked against build v26.43.5-77de68c (production) on 11/2/2026.
